transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you too, Dr. Smith. Well, I suppose... I mean, my wife is the one who really pushed for this appointment. We've been having some friction at home lately, and it all really revolves around her job. She works in this office downtown, and for the past year—exactly a year, really, starting right around last October—she's been having all these late meetings. 

And, look, I’m a teaching assistant at the university, I’m in a graduate program, so I completely understand working late and having an unpredictable schedule. I grade papers until midnight all the time. But it’s... it’s the way she texts me when she’s at these meetings. She says the little changes in her work messages to me are just normal office stuff, just her being rushed or autocorrect or whatever excuse she has that day. But if you actually sit down and look at them, the way I have, they’ve lined up just way too precisely to feel accidental. 

It’s not just a typo here and there. It’s... well, it’s like there’s a private signal in them, you know? Like the specific words she chooses are meant to tell me something she just won’t come out and say directly to my face. I've tried to show her the patterns, how the phrasing shifts on certain days of the week, but she just brushes it off and tells me I'm overthinking it and that I need to talk to a professional. Which is why I'm sitting here, honestly, even though I think anyone who actually took the time to look at the messages side-by-side would see exactly what I'm talking about.

Aside from these messages, have you noticed any other unusual experiences, such as hearing sounds or voices that others don't seem to hear, or noticing things that feel like they have a special, personal meaning just for you?

No, no, nothing like that. I mean, I don't hear voices or... or see things that aren't there, if that's what you're getting at. My hearing is perfectly fine. Actually, it's funny you mention hearing, because the acoustics in the lecture hall where I TA are just awful, and I have to strain to hear the students in the back row all the time, but that's just poor architectural design, not... not anything going on in my head. 

And as for things having a special meaning... well, I mean, the texts *do* have a special meaning, but that's because they're coming from my wife, and she's specifically sending them to my phone. It's not like I'm walking down the street and thinking the license plates on the cars are trying to communicate with me, or that the news anchor on TV is blinking in Morse code just for my benefit. I'm a rational person, Dr. Smith. I'm in a graduate program, I grade research papers, I understand the difference between a coincidence and a statistically significant pattern. 

I don't think the universe is sending me signs. I just think my wife is sending me very specific, very deliberate text messages. It's all contained right there in the phone, in the actual data. If I were hearing voices, I think I'd be the first one to say, "Okay, maybe I need some help here." But this is just... it's just about the texts. Just the texts and the way the wording changes on Tuesdays and Thursdays when she has those specific meetings. That's really the whole of it.
